subject: Post-call: structured-output & tool-calling evals for Ava Software
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@avasw.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — structured output + tool-calling requirements

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track actions: 

Recap
- Goal: Automate invoice ingestion and downstream extraction into accounting system via a tool-calling flow (JSON output -> webhook -> internal processor).
- Key non-functional requirements: 99th pct latency < 700ms for single-request extractions (SLA target), 50 qps sustained burst for batch ingestion, strict JSON schema compliance for downstream processor, and a retry policy for transient parsing failures.
- Primary quality concern you raised: regression risk when model updates affect field boundary detection (addresses, line items).

Proposed next steps
1) Evaluation run (we run a controlled eval on your sample set): I can coordinate a 72-hour run against 2 model configs. Need your sample data and a decision on whether PII should be redacted prior to upload.
2) Schema & prompt pack: attached is our initial prompt_set_v1.txt and initial_schema_v1.json — please confirm schema fields and any mandatory validation rules.
3) Benchmarks & thresholds: we will run precision/recall on required fields and produce a per-field F1 baseline. Target: >= 0.92 F1 for invoice_number, >= 0.88 for line_items with tolerance bands.
4) Tool-calling behavior & retries: we recommend a two-stage strategy — (A) enforced JSON schema validation in the runtime with schema-based rejection and (B) a retry with augmented prompts + caching of previous good KV if transient. Details below.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt, initial_schema_v1.json

Questions for you
- Can you share a representative sample of 200–500 invoices (PDFs or CSV)?
- Is a 48–72 hour window for the initial eval acceptable?
- Any additional fields that must be strictly exact (e.g., tax_id)?

I’ll wait on the sample files and will schedule a short scoping call with Karthik and Vanessa to align on the technical checklist.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1-415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — structured output + tool-calling requirements

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the concise recap — this captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can share 300 invoices in CSV and the original PDFs; I attached a 10-row sample (sample_invoices.csv) to this reply.
- Latency target: 700ms 99th is accurate for single-document extraction; for batch throughput the system should be able to sustain 30–40 qps initially.
- For PII: we prefer to redact only customer emails and full credit card numbers, but keep addresses and tax_ids intact for matching.

Questions: 
- Will the eval run against the same model version for the full 72 hours, or do you rotate variants? We want a consistent baseline.
- What does your rollback plan look like if we see quality regressions after a model update?

We’re available for a 30-minute scoping call tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Product Manager, Ava Software
emily.chen@avasw.com

Attachment: sample_invoices.csv (CSV, 10 rows)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@avasw.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — structured output + tool-calling requirements

Emily — great, thanks for the sample and the redaction guidance. Short answers:

Eval rotation policy
- For the initial baseline we will run a single pinned model variant for 72 hours to get a stable baseline (Model A). After baseline completes we can run Model B for comparison in a separate run window. We won’t rotate models mid-run unless you ask us to.

Rollback / regression policy
- Redwood supports pinned model versions per-route. If a model update causes regression we can automatically roll back to the pinned variant. Additionally, we can configure an automatic quality-gate tied to your prompt set: if per-field F1 drops > 3pts vs baseline we trigger rollback and page the team.

Recommended model candidates (based on your latency/throughput needs and structured-output focus)
- opt-instruct-13b (quantized int8) — good precision, lower RAM; expect ~200–350ms median token latency on our hosted us-west GPU pool for single extractions and reliable structured output with few-shot prompts.
- rw-instruct-7b (optimized for JSON-schema output) — faster, cheaper, slightly lower recall on nested line items; useful as a low-cost baseline in Dedicated mode.

Benchmarks & links
- Baseline run plan and thresholds: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/ava-evals
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678 (RD-AVA-2026-101)

Attachments: eval_checklist.pdf (checklist we’ll use to validate runs)

Proposed immediate actions
1) Confirm we have permission to ingest the 300 files to our secure eval bucket (we redact only per your spec).
2) Sign off on schema (if any required fields are missing please annotate initial_schema_v1.json).
3) Schedule the 30-minute scoping call with Karthik and Vanessa tomorrow 9:30–10:00 PST — I’ll send a calendar invite.

We’ll also include a short test harness that exercises function-calling retry scenarios (simulate a schema validation failure and validate retry + prompt augmentation behavior).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik for technical details in the call.

Best,
Logan

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@avasw.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Technical checklist & schema fuzz plan prior to eval run

Hi Emily — looping in the engineering checklist we discussed so it’s actionable after the scoping call. Short version + concrete steps: 

1) Schema validation harness
- We run initial_schema_v1.json against 1,000 synthetic mutations to ensure the runtime validator flags required-field errors. The harness will produce an error-rate matrix by field.
- Deliverable: schema_fuzz_plan.md (attached) with exact mutation rules (truncation, type swap, missing nested arrays).

2) Function-calling / retry test scenarios
- Scenario A: Schema rejection on first-call -> attempt 1 automated retry with prompt augmentation (explicit fill-in instructions and two-shot example) -> if still invalid, forward to human-in-loop webhook.
- Scenario B: KV-cache enabled: repeated requests with identical prefixes should return cached tokens for deterministic fields (invoice_number, vendor_id).

3) Quality regression detection thresholds
- Per-field F1 drop > 3 percentage points from baseline triggers rollback and Slack paging.
- Line-item level: if NER-based token overlap < 0.80 we flag for manual review.

4) Acceptance criteria for go/no-go
- Mandatory: invoice_number F1 >= 0.92, line_items F1 >= 0.88, schema validation pass rate >= 98% on sample set.

5) Quick verification curl (example)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"opt-instruct-13b","input":"<invoice_pdf_base64>","response_format":{"type":"json_schema","schema_url":"https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/initial_schema_v1.json"}}'

Next steps for scheduling: if we land on tomorrow’s 9:30 PST slot I’ll run a short demo of the fuzz harness and show the test harness that simulates retries.

Attaching: schema_fuzz_plan.md

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
